name: Recovery Spin 30
desc: Thirty minutes of very easy pedalling to promote blood flow without adding training stress. Keep it conversational and spin light at 85-95 rpm; it should feel easier than you think it should.

name: Recovery Spin 45
desc: A slightly longer active recovery ride with a few gentle cadence pickups to keep the legs supple. All efforts stay well inside Zone 1 so you recover for the next quality day.
src: Classic Coggan active recovery (Zone 1) with cadence pickups

name: Recovery Flush 60
desc: An hour at the top of the recovery zone for riders who want time on the bike on a rest day. Smooth, steady pedalling at 0.50-0.55 with relaxed upper body; no surges.
src: Recovery ride / flush ride convention used in pro team plans

name: Endurance 45
desc: A short aerobic base ride in Zone 2. Ride steady at 65-70% FTP with smooth pedalling; builds mitochondrial density and fat oxidation with minimal fatigue.

name: Endurance 60
desc: One hour of steady Zone 2 with a gentle progression from low to mid endurance. Keep breathing easy and nasal if possible; the goal is aerobic volume, not intensity.

name: Endurance 90
desc: A 90-minute aerobic ride with brief cadence changes every 15 minutes to break up the monotony. Stay at 65-72% FTP; this is the bread-and-butter session for base building.

name: Endurance 2h
desc: Two hours of steady aerobic riding for long-ride durability. Hold 65-72% FTP, fuel every 20-30 minutes and stand for 30 seconds every so often to stay comfortable.
src: Long slow distance / Zone 2 base (Seiler polarized model)

name: Endurance 3h
desc: A long indoor base ride for building aerobic endurance and fatigue resistance. Ride steady in Zone 2, finishing the last 20 minutes at the top of the zone; fuel and hydrate as for an outdoor long ride.
src: Long slow distance / Zone 2 base (Seiler polarized model)

name: Progressive Endurance 75
desc: A Zone 2 ride that steps up gently every 15 minutes, finishing near the top of endurance. Teaches pacing and builds aerobic durability as fatigue accumulates.

name: Cadence Pyramid
desc: An endurance ride with cadence pyramids at constant Zone 2 power. Climb from 85 to 115 rpm and back while keeping hips stable and no bouncing; improves pedalling economy and neuromuscular coordination.
src: Classic cadence pyramid drill (base-period skill work)

name: High-Cadence Spin-Ups
desc: Zone 2 ride with progressive spin-ups to 120+ rpm at light load. Increase cadence over each effort while staying smooth in the saddle; trains neuromuscular speed and smooth stroke.
src: Classic spin-up drill (Friel base period skills)

name: Isolated-Leg Focus
desc: Endurance ride with alternating single-leg-focus blocks: put emphasis on one leg (other leg just along for the ride) at high cadence, then the other, then both. Clean pull-through at the bottom and over the top; ERG holds low power so the drill stays technical.
src: Single-leg drill adapted for smart trainers (Friel / Carmichael pedalling drills)

name: Low-Cadence Strength Endurance
desc: Aerobic ride with seated low-cadence blocks at upper Zone 2 / low tempo. Stay seated, quiet upper body and drive through the whole stroke; builds muscular endurance with low cardiovascular cost.
src: Torque / strength-endurance intervals (Rønnestad low-cadence work, Spanish "fuerza" blocks)

name: Tempo 3x10
desc: Introductory tempo session: three 10-minute blocks at 80% FTP. Comfortably hard, controlled breathing; builds aerobic power and muscular endurance.

name: Tempo 2x20
desc: Two 20-minute tempo blocks at 80-83% FTP. Settle in, stay seated and hold steady cadence; a staple for building aerobic engine and fatigue resistance.

name: Tempo Hour
desc: A long sustained tempo block within an endurance ride: 45 continuous minutes at 78-82% FTP with cadence variation every 15 minutes. Excellent for gran fondo and time-trial preparation.

name: Tempo with Bursts
desc: Three 12-minute tempo blocks with a 15-second hard surge every 2 minutes. Surge out of the saddle, then settle straight back to tempo; simulates race surges and teaches lactate clearance at moderate intensity.

name: Tempo Surges 2x20
desc: Two 20-minute tempo blocks with a 30-second surge to 120% every 4 minutes. The surges spike lactate; the tempo that follows forces you to clear it while still working.

name: Low-Cadence Tempo 4x10
desc: Four 10-minute seated tempo blocks at 65 rpm. Builds torque and muscular endurance useful for climbing and time-trialling; keep the core quiet and avoid rocking.

name: Sweet Spot 4x8
desc: Entry-level sweet spot: four 8-minute efforts at 88% FTP. Strong but sustainable; builds FTP with less fatigue than threshold work. A good first step before longer sweet spot intervals.
src: Sweet spot training concept (Coggan / Sweet Spot "88-94%")

name: Sweet Spot 3x10
desc: Three 10-minute sweet spot efforts at 88-90% FTP. Settle into a rhythm and hold steady cadence; a bridge between introductory and classic sweet spot sessions.

name: Sweet Spot 4x12
desc: Four 12-minute efforts at 90% FTP with short recoveries. Accumulates 48 minutes of time-in-zone to raise FTP and muscular endurance.

name: Sweet Spot 3x15
desc: Three 15-minute efforts at 90% FTP. Stay seated and relaxed, fuel before the session; a classic mid-progression sweet spot workout.

name: Sweet Spot 2x20
desc: The classic sweet spot session: two 20-minute efforts at 88-90% FTP. Builds sustainable power and muscular endurance; aim for even pacing and steady cadence throughout.
src: Classic 2x20 sweet spot (Coggan / Allen & Coggan "Training and Racing with a Power Meter")

name: Sweet Spot 3x20
desc: Three 20-minute efforts at 90% FTP: an hour of quality sweet spot work. A demanding session for experienced riders building towards longer events; fuel during the recoveries.

name: Sweet Spot 2x30
desc: Two 30-minute efforts at 88% FTP. Long intervals develop fatigue resistance and mental focus; pace the first 10 minutes conservatively and stay fuelled.
src: Extended sweet spot (Coggan sweet spot progression)

name: Sweet Spot 45
desc: A single 45-minute sweet spot block at 87-89% FTP. Simulates a sustained climb or time-trial effort; split it mentally into thirds and vary cadence slightly in each.
src: Long sweet spot block (Coggan sweet spot progression)

name: Sweet Spot Progression
desc: Three 15-minute efforts, each stepping up through the sweet spot range: 86% to 90% to 94%. Builds pacing discipline and pushes the top end of sweet spot as fatigue rises.
src: Sweet spot step progression (common coach structure)

name: Sweet Spot with Bursts
desc: Three 12-minute sweet spot intervals with a 15-second kick at 150% every 3 minutes. The bursts recruit fast-twitch fibres and add lactate that must be cleared at sweet spot; very race-specific.

name: Sweet Spot Tempo Blend
desc: Alternating 10-minute sweet spot and 5-minute tempo blocks for 60 minutes without full recovery. Keeps intensity high without going over threshold; builds big aerobic volume.

name: Threshold 5x6
desc: Five 6-minute efforts at 98-100% FTP with equal-ish recovery. A gentle entry into threshold work; focus on smooth, even power and controlled breathing.

name: Threshold 5x8
desc: Five 8-minute efforts at 100% FTP. Builds lactate threshold and the ability to sustain hard efforts; ride just at threshold, not over it.

name: Threshold 3x10
desc: Three 10-minute efforts at FTP. A staple threshold session that develops the ability to hold race pace on climbs and breakaways.

name: Threshold 4x10
desc: Four 10-minute efforts at 98-100% FTP with 4 minutes recovery. Forty minutes of time at threshold for raising FTP; stay seated and steady.

name: Threshold 3x12
desc: Three 12-minute efforts at 98-100% FTP. A step up in interval length; aim to finish the last one strong without fading.

name: Threshold 2x15
desc: Two 15-minute efforts at FTP. Bridges between 10-minute intervals and the classic 2x20; requires pacing discipline and mental focus.

name: Threshold 2x20
desc: The benchmark FTP session: two 20-minute efforts at 95-100% FTP. Raises lactate threshold and sustainable power; the gold standard for time-trial and climbing fitness.

name: Threshold 40
desc: A single 40-minute effort at 95% FTP: time-trial simulation. Start controlled, settle in, and hold even power to the end; trains sustainable power and pacing.
src: Long threshold block / 40 km TT simulation (Coggan)

name: Threshold 6x5
desc: Six 5-minute efforts at 102% FTP with 2.5-minute recoveries. Slightly above FTP with short rest; builds tolerance to threshold-level effort.

name: Threshold Ladder
desc: A ladder of threshold efforts: 4, 6, 8, 10, 8, 6, 4 minutes at 98-102% FTP. Longer efforts sit slightly below FTP and shorter ones slightly above; builds pacing across durations.

name: Progressive Threshold 3x12
desc: Three 12-minute efforts each built in three 4-minute steps: 95%, 100%, 105% FTP. Teaches negative-split pacing and finishing hard when fatigued.

name: Over-Unders 3x9
desc: Three 9-minute blocks alternating 2 minutes at 95% and 1 minute at 105% FTP. The overs generate lactate; the unders teach the body to process it while still working near threshold.

name: Over-Unders 4x10
desc: Four 10-minute blocks of 2 min at 95% / 1 min at 105% FTP, finishing each with an extra minute under. Progresses the 3x9 session with more time at and around threshold.

name: Over-Unders 90/110
desc: Three 12-minute blocks alternating 2 minutes at 90% and 1 minute at 110% FTP. Bigger swings than 95/105: the overs push well past threshold and the unders recover only partially.

name: Over-Unders with Surges
desc: Three 10-minute blocks at 92% FTP with a 30-second surge to 120% every 2 minutes. Mimics attacks on a climb; the surges are short and sharp, the floor stays high.

name: Criss-Cross 2x20
desc: Two 20-minute efforts at 88% FTP with a 1-minute rise to 105% every 4 minutes. A sweet spot base with threshold-crossing surges; builds the ability to respond to pace changes and recover on the go.

name: Over-Under Progression
desc: Four 8-minute blocks where each 1-minute over at 108% is followed by a 1-minute under at 92-96%, with the unders rising across the set. Fatigue builds steadily, ending as an advanced lactate-tolerance session.
src: Progressive over-unders (coach structure building on Carmichael over-unders)
